title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an artificial intelligence scribe transcribe her first appointment with a urologist in Australia. The tool falsely recorded that she used psychedelic mushrooms, and this claim appeared in a post-operative letter after her kidney stone surgery in March. She discovered the error only by reading the letter sent to her GP and worried it could affect her workers’ compensation case. After she complained, the urologist apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used, but did not answer questions about any changes. A privacy group found similar mistakes, such as recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates about 40 percent of GPs regularly use AI scribes.

The Therapeutic Goods Administration has been reviewing AI scribes and says its findings will be released in the coming weeks, with any breaches acted upon. Digital Rights Watch wants the new AI Safety Institute to test these tools and publish a list of approved products. Ms Green said she would only consent to AI transcription again if she had an established relationship with the doctor.
